newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says it took delivery of third submarine.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it took delivery of third submarine.

text.p: Iran said it had taken delivery of a new Russian-made submarine which military analysts say will boost the Islamic republic's naval power in the Gulf, the world's largest oil-export route.
"The third Iranian submarine joined in a ceremony on Monday...the navy in Bandar Abbas," said an army statement published in Iranian newspapers on Thursday. It did not give other details.
It was the first word from Iran on the arrival of the Russian-made submarine, which Western military officials said had entered Iran's waters on January 18.

Non-Arab Iran already has two Russian-made submarines and analysts say it has poured billions of dollars into its navy since the end of the eight-year Iran-Iraq war in 1988. This has raised concerns in oil-rich Gulf Arab states, which the United States has vowed to protect.
Iran, which has said arms purchases are for self-defence, is the only Gulf state with submarines. The first of the three submarines was delivered to Iran in November 1992 and the second in June 1993.
Military analysts said the new ship would enhance Iran's ability to control Gulf waterways. It can lay mines and fire torpedoes against ships in the Gulf.
